analyst_view.overall: Lecce (15th, 10 points, LLLDL, 3-0 loser at Lazio last time) host Atalanta (12th, 15 points, 4-4 with Inter on 23 November) on Monday evening; the numbers make Atalanta clear favourites. Eusebio Di Francesco's Lecce are in the relegation fight and miss Kaba, Ilic and Pierotti, all counted by the numbers; Veiga and Siebert are one booking from a ban. Maurizio Sarri's Atalanta, publicly backed by the club but judged on results, played away at Borac Banja Luka in the Conference League on Thursday with a heavily rotated side, so most first choices should be fresher; Carnesecchi is out after knee surgery (counted) with Sportiello in goal. Sarri called his defence the weakest unit, and Hien, Kossounou and Pompei trained apart this week, which the numbers do not count. The referee is Mattia Drigo.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.8 for Atalanta, already counting Ilic out for Lecce, Carnesecchi out for Atalanta and Atalanta's 12 conceded in six. Sarri himself called his defence the weakest unit, and centre-backs Hien and Kossounou were training apart this week, which the numbers don't see; one report only for their status, so I lean just a little higher (+3%), about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already raised for Atalanta's 36 corners conceded in six. Lecce's 4-3-3 with N'Dri and Fatah wide and Atalanta's 4-2-3-1 with Bellanova and Zappacosta pushing on are their usual shapes, so nothing new points either way; I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards, raised about 9% because Atalanta's recent opponents picked up 16 cards in six, and trimmed for the head-to-head. A home side in a relegation fight can get edgy, but Veiga and Siebert, one booking from a ban, may play more carefully, and I found nothing on referee Mattia Drigo's style, so I stay at about 3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots, already lifted 16% for Lecce's 82 shots in six against an Atalanta side that allows plenty (96 in six). Atalanta's rotation in Bosnia should leave Kessie, De Ketelaere and Krstovic fresh, and Lecce have had a full week, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target, already raised for both sides' recent accuracy (Lecce +14%, Atalanta +3%). Atalanta's attack should be close to full strength after resting players on Thursday, and Lecce's front line of Geubbels or Stulic is unchanged, so I stay at about 9.5.
